```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.8)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(caret))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(randomForest))
```

## Question and data

The task is to predict **how** a participant performed a barbell lift. The
outcome `classe` has five categories (A to E). I used the [provided training
data](https://d396qusza40orc.cloudfront.net/predmachlearn/pml-training.csv) for
model building and kept the [20-case test
set](https://d396qusza40orc.cloudfront.net/predmachlearn/pml-testing.csv) for
the final quiz predictions. The original [Weight Lifting Exercises data
source](https://web.archive.org/web/20161224072740/http://groupware.les.inf.puc-rio.br/har)
describes the sensor study.

## Prepare the data

These commands download the CSV files only if they are absent from the current
project folder. Blank values, `NA`, and `#DIV/0!` are treated as missing.

```{r data}
train_url <- "https://d396qusza40orc.cloudfront.net/predmachlearn/pml-training.csv"
test_url  <- "https://d396qusza40orc.cloudfront.net/predmachlearn/pml-testing.csv"

if (!file.exists("pml-training.csv")) {
  download.file(train_url, "pml-training.csv", mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
}
if (!file.exists("pml-testing.csv")) {
  download.file(test_url, "pml-testing.csv", mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
}

training <- read.csv("pml-training.csv",
                     na.strings = c("NA", "", "#DIV/0!"))
testing <- read.csv("pml-testing.csv",
                    na.strings = c("NA", "", "#DIV/0!"))
stopifnot("classe" %in% names(training), nrow(testing) == 20)
training$classe <- factor(training$classe)

# Row identifiers, participant names, dates and window labels are not sensor
# measurements. Exclude them to avoid learning a shortcut unrelated to motion.
metadata <- c("X", "user_name", "raw_timestamp_part_1",
              "raw_timestamp_part_2", "cvtd_timestamp", "new_window",
              "num_window", "problem_id")
shared <- setdiff(intersect(names(training), names(testing)), metadata)

# Use only numeric sensor columns that have values in every row of both sets.
complete_numeric <- function(nm) {
  is.numeric(training[[nm]]) && is.numeric(testing[[nm]]) &&
    all(is.finite(training[[nm]])) && all(is.finite(testing[[nm]]))
}
predictors <- shared[vapply(shared, complete_numeric, logical(1))]
stopifnot(length(predictors) > 0)

# Remove constant or nearly constant predictors based on training data only.
nzv <- caret::nearZeroVar(training[, predictors, drop = FALSE])
if (length(nzv) > 0) predictors <- predictors[-nzv]
stopifnot(length(predictors) > 0)

data.frame(training_rows = nrow(training), test_rows = nrow(testing),
           sensor_predictors = length(predictors))
```

This leaves `r length(predictors)` complete numeric sensor predictors. I did
not use the 20 test cases to tune the model or estimate accuracy, because their
true labels are unavailable.

## Cross validation and model selection

I used a stratified 75% split for model development and reserved 25% as an
untouched validation set. Within the development set, three-fold cross
validation compared two values of `mtry`, the number of sensor variables
considered at each random forest split. Accuracy selected the better value.
The random seed makes the split and fitting repeatable.

```{r fit, cache=TRUE}
set.seed(2026)
development_rows <- caret::createDataPartition(training$classe, p = 0.75,
                                               list = FALSE)
development <- training[development_rows, , drop = FALSE]
validation <- training[-development_rows, , drop = FALSE]

mtry_values <- sort(unique(pmin(length(predictors), c(6L, 12L))))
folds <- caret::trainControl(method = "cv", number = 3,
                            allowParallel = FALSE)
set.seed(2026)
cv_model <- caret::train(
  x = development[, predictors, drop = FALSE],
  y = development$classe,
  method = "rf",
  trControl = folds,
  tuneGrid = data.frame(mtry = mtry_values),
  metric = "Accuracy",
  ntree = 150
)

knitr::kable(cv_model$results[, c("mtry", "Accuracy", "AccuracySD")],
             digits = 4, caption = "Accuracy across the three folds")
```

The selected `mtry` is `r cv_model$bestTune$mtry`. The folds estimate model
performance inside the development set; the separate validation set gives a
more direct check of the selected model.

## Validation and expected error

```{r validation}
validation_pred <- predict(cv_model,
                           newdata = validation[, predictors, drop = FALSE])
cm <- caret::confusionMatrix(validation_pred, validation$classe)
accuracy <- unname(cm$overall["Accuracy"])
error_rate <- 1 - accuracy

knitr::kable(as.data.frame.matrix(cm$table),
             caption = "Validation confusion matrix: predicted class by actual class")
data.frame(validation_cases = nrow(validation),
           accuracy = round(accuracy, 4),
           estimated_error_rate = round(error_rate, 4))
```

The model correctly classified `r sum(validation_pred == validation$classe)`
of `r nrow(validation)` reserved records. Validation accuracy was
`r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * accuracy)`; the estimated out-of-sample error was
`r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * error_rate)`. This estimate applies most directly
to similar records from this study. Since the same six people can appear in
both portions of a row-level split, accuracy for entirely new people could
be lower.

## Final model and 20 quiz answers

With the settings chosen above, I refitted the forest on all labeled rows.
The 20 test records were used only here, after the validation result was fixed.

```{r final-model}
set.seed(2026)
final_model <- randomForest::randomForest(
  x = training[, predictors, drop = FALSE],
  y = training$classe,
  mtry = cv_model$bestTune$mtry,
  ntree = 150,
  importance = TRUE
)
quiz_prediction <- predict(final_model,
                           newdata = testing[, predictors, drop = FALSE],
                           type = "class")

quiz_id <- if ("problem_id" %in% names(testing)) {
  testing$problem_id
} else {
  seq_len(nrow(testing))
}
answers <- data.frame(problem_id = quiz_id,
                      prediction = as.character(quiz_prediction))
stopifnot(nrow(answers) == 20, all(answers$prediction %in% levels(training$classe)))
write.csv(answers, "predictions.csv", row.names = FALSE)
writeLines(answers$prediction, "prediction_answers.txt")

knitr::kable(answers, caption = "Submit these predictions in problem order")
```

The answers are also saved in `predictions.csv` and, one per line, in
`prediction_answers.txt` in the project folder. Check the problem number before
entering each answer in the prediction quiz.

```{r importance, echo=FALSE}
randomForest::varImpPlot(final_model, n.var = 12,
                         main = "Most influential sensor measurements")
```

## Reproduce the analysis

Open this `.Rmd` in RStudio and click **Knit**. Running it again will use the
same saved CSV files and random seed. Package versions used in this run:
`caret` `r as.character(packageVersion("caret"))` and `randomForest`
`r as.character(packageVersion("randomForest"))` on
`r R.version.string`.
